summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a number.
description: `nonNumber(value)` is the same test as `!isNumber(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
The test is `typeof value === "number"`, which `NaN` and both infinities satisfy. Use `isFloat`, `isInteger` or `isNaN` when those cases have to be told apart.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a number; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonNumber("1"); // => true
nonNumber(null); // => true
nonNumber(0); // => false
nonNumber(1.5); // => false
nonNumber(NaN); // => false
nonNumber(Infinity); // => false
```
